name: Abominable Creatures

angles.text: Human adventurers witness the heartbreaking fate of Lordaeron's fallen leadership, as even an esteemed Grand Marshal was transformed into a grotesque undead horror. Captain Truman's bitter grief and nationalistic zeal reflect the raw trauma carried by human survivors desperate to reclaim their ancestral home.

The quest highlights the perilous, isolated plight of Alliance-aligned remnants trying to operate within the blighted ruins of northern Lordaeron. It emphasizes how lingering loyalist detachments struggle with dwindling hope and the psychological toll of fighting overwhelming monstrosities.

For the Forsaken, the Baron's grotesque transformation is a grim reminder of how the Scourge mutilated Lordaeron's finest defenders into monstrous abominations. Captain Truman's vow to purge the ruins of all beasts and undead reflects the relentless hostility living loyalists hold against the Undercity's people.

faq.answer: The quest is offered by Captain Truman, a human loyalist stationed in the region surrounding the fallen kingdom. Anxiously holding his post while awaiting reinforcements, Truman desperately seeks news of his commander, a revered Grand Marshal who charged into the nearby Ruins of Lordaeron.
faq.q: Who gives the quest Abominable Creatures?

faq.answer: The quest directs adventurers into the Ruins of Lordaeron, the shattered capital city overrun by Scourge horrors and undead remnants. Captain Truman maintains a post outside the blighted capital, asking brave travelers to venture directly into the dangerous ruins to locate his missing superior.
faq.q: Where does the quest Abominable Creatures take place?

faq.answer: Captain Truman refers to his master as the Grand Marshal, praising him as a tall, statuesque military hero. However, the quest objectives refer to this missing noble as the Baron, indicating that he was a high-ranking aristocrat and military commander leading the defense of the realm.

Rather than holding out victoriously, the Grand Marshal was slain and transformed into a monstrous undead creature within the Ruins of Lordaeron. When adventurers locate him, they find an abomination designated as the Baron, forcing them to destroy him and claim his severed head.
faq.q: What happened to the Grand Marshal in the Ruins of Lordaeron?

aliases: why does truman yell at you
faq.answer: Captain Truman expected his statuesque commander to be alive and victorious. When presented with the grotesque, mutated head of the Baron, Truman is overcome with horror and revulsion, furiously accusing the adventurer of playing a sick joke and consorting with vile beasts.
faq.q: Why does Captain Truman get angry when you turn in the quest?

aliases: who are the true sons of lordaeron
faq.answer: Captain Truman uses the term to describe zealous human patriots dedicated to reclaiming their shattered homeland. His words express a fierce, intolerant vision where the rightful human survivors will purge the kingdom of all undead, beasts, and anyone perceived as consorting with them.
faq.q: What does Captain Truman mean by the 'true sons of Lordaeron'?

faq.answer: Captain Truman displays deep disdain for non-human races and irregular allies, dismissing them as untrustworthy half-breeds and filth. His intense xenophobia prevents him from confiding in anyone other than those he deems worthy representatives of the realm.
faq.q: Why does Captain Truman refuse to trust 'half breeds'?

sections.body: Captain Truman stands vigilant at his post, anxiously awaiting long-overdue reinforcements to support the defense of Lordaeron. Confident in the martial prowess of his superior—a renowned Grand Marshal whom he describes as a tall, statuesque hero—Truman remains bound by duty after being commanded to hold the line while his commander charged into the ongoing fray. Harboring deep suspicion toward outsiders and openly scorning those he considers lesser breeds, the captain refuses to trust local irregulars. When a capable traveler approaches, Truman seizes the opportunity to enlist aid, pleading for someone to venture into the ruined territory to check on his master's well-being and assess the battle.
sections.title: A Desperate Vigil

sections.body: The search directs adventurers straight into the perilous Ruins of Lordaeron, the shattered capital that fell to the Scourge during the Third War. Although Captain Truman expects his glorious leader to be standing triumphant over the fallen, the reality within the blighted city is far grimmer. The ruins are overrun with horrors, undead remnants, and abominations wandering the broken stone plazas. Navigating these devastated streets requires confronting the brutal truth of what happened to the defenders who ventured into the city. Instead of finding an immaculate knight holding the line, travelers discover that the commander has met a tragic, twisted end among the monstrosities occupying the courtyards.
sections.title: The Ruins of Lordaeron

sections.body: Upon locating the missing commander, designated as the Baron, adventurers make a horrifying discovery: the once-statuesque hero has been transformed into a grotesque undead monstrosity. Fulfilling the grim task requires slaying the creature and taking the Head of the Baron back to Captain Truman. When presented with the severed head of his former lord, Truman reacts with shock, horror, and profound revulsion. Unable to accept the dreadful fate of his commander, the captain lashes out in bitter outrage, accusing the adventurer of being in league with monsters and vowing that the true sons of Lordaeron will one day reclaim their land and purge all beasts.
sections.title: A Horrifying Revelation

summary: Abominable Creatures is a quest given by Captain Truman, a human loyalist desperately awaiting reinforcements on the outskirts of Lordaeron's fallen capital. Believing his commander—a revered Grand Marshal—is still valiantly fighting in the nearby Ruins of Lordaeron, Truman implores a capable adventurer to track him down. The mission exposes the grim fate of the kingdom's lost defenders and the bitter hostility smoldering among surviving loyalists.
